name: Induction motor (rotating magnetic field)
description: Parametric explode of a polyphase induction motor: frame → stator → windings → air gap → rotor cage → shaft → load. Live per-phase equivalent-circuit HUD. [Known] CONCEPT-MATH §2.1.

layers.label: Windings
layers.description: Spatially offset phase belts (2- or 3-phase approx).

layers.label: Air gap
layers.description: Thin translucent cylindrical spacer — magnetic gap g.

layers.label: Rotor cage
layers.description: Cylinder + end rings + bar approximations (squirrel cage).

layers.label: Load
layers.description: Simple disk / flywheel on shaft end.

equations.notes: Synchronous speed of the rotating field. f in Hz, p = pole count (even).
Operating slip solved so developed torque matches T_load (steady-state).

equations.latex: T = (3 p / (2 \omega_s)) * (s R_2 V^2) / (R_2^2 + (s X_2)^2)   [Estimate scale]
equations.plaintext: T_phase_shape = s*R2*V^2 / (R2^2 + (s*X2)^2);  T = K * T_phase_shape with K = (3*p)/(4*pi*f) so that units are N·m for a 3-phase approx. Stator R1,X1 omitted from torque peak location (classic rotor-limited approx). [Estimate]
equations.notes: Per-phase Thevenin/rotor branch shape from CONCEPT-MATH §2.1. Constant K chosen so T has N·m for SI ohm/volt inputs under a 3-phase teaching model. Not a full IEEE 112 test curve.

equations.plaintext: Pout = T * (2*pi*n/60); Pin ≈ 3 * (V^2 * (s*R2) / (R2^2+(s*X2)^2)) air-gap power proxy; η = Pout/Pin when Pin>0. [Estimate]
equations.notes: Pin here is an air-gap power proxy from the rotor branch (ignores stator copper + core). Labelled Estimate.

myth_notes: Ferraris demonstrated a rotating field independently (priority dispute). Industry adopted 3-phase; Tesla's early demos were often 2-phase. No free-energy claim — COP < 1 always for this machine. See 08-speculative-vs-verified.md.
